harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent 389 Directory Server on node1 with the supplied HR record, trusted LDAPS access restricted to node2, field-level employeeNumber privacy, dedicated root-only reader/admin credentials, and successful sequential reboot recovery on both nodes.
actions_performed: Installed supported RHEL 10 directory-server and LDAP client packages without changing the OS release or kernel.
Loaded and preserved the supplied HR LDIF.
Created node-generated directory-reader and HR-administrator credentials; stored them in mode-0600 files without exposing their values.
Configured reader access to employee names and mail only, HR-administrator write access, and no anonymous employee visibility.
Restricted LDAPS ingress to node2's address; retained SELinux enforcing and firewalld active.
Tested allowed reads, denied employeeNumber reads/writes, administrator modification and restoration, and anonymous denial.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities plus complete recovery.
Removed temporary transfer keys, duplicate secret copies, test LDIFs, and other working artifacts.

evidence.requirement: Supplied LDIF loaded and retained unchanged
evidence.summary: The retained source SHA-256 remained bbfcee87cc16fcfc5e85ece5fbe78b048b3363cb93eb4bc37fee7940508dd10f, and final LDAP fields match it.

evidence.requirement: Reader can search employee names and mail from node2 but cannot read or change employeeNumber
evidence.summary: Remote reader searches returned Morgan Lake and morgan@hr.test, returned zero employeeNumber values, and writes failed with LDAP insufficient-access result 50.

evidence.requirement: Only the HR administrator may read or change employeeNumber
evidence.summary: The HR administrator read and changed employeeNumber successfully, the reader was denied, and the original value was restored. Final ACI audit shows the two narrowly scoped policies.

evidence.requirement: Anonymous users see no employee records
evidence.summary: Anonymous employee-search count remained zero before and after both restarts.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated demonstration credentials are securely provisioned
evidence.summary: Administrator and reader credential files are root-owned mode 0600, LDAP passwords are stored hashed, and temporary transfer credentials are absent.

evidence.requirement: Network and host security remain narrowly scoped
evidence.summary: Only node2/32 is permitted to the LDAPS service; SELinux is Enforcing, firewalld is active, and both nodes report zero failed units.

evidence.requirement: Compatible software used without replacing OS or kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0; native RHEL packages provide 389-ds-base 3.2.0 and OpenLDAP clients 2.6.10.
Boot ID changed from 180a78a0-8a84-45ff-82f1-cd734208a369 to 4a7b930c-3c31-4799-a470-000cb0ad8eb8; directory service, firewall, data, reader access, privacy controls, and anonymous denial recovered.

Boot ID changed from 739c9792-2418-47cc-a875-95b27428f3fc to b38061e3-ef20-40ef-b12a-9985f2c11ba9; the reader credential, remote workflow, denied write, anonymous denial, source data, and node1 service remained healthy.

attempts.summary: Configured a persistent 389 Directory Server on node1 with the supplied HR record, trusted LDAPS access restricted to node2, field-level employeeNumber privacy, dedicated root-only reader/admin credentials, and successful sequential reboot recovery on both nodes.
